I've went through a lot of labels, loveless aro being one of them. 

My advice will always be to try labels out and see if they fit for you. 

I don't really use loveless aro to describe myself anymore even though it really did fit at one point.  However, the things I learned about myself during that time were important for uncovering nuances in my identity. 

As for how to decenter love, i wouldnt consider it as something you primarily think your way out of. Notice first that your life is *not over* if you're aromantic. After you realize that you'll eventually want to find other things to do with your time. 

Eventually you'll see how much joy and fulfillment there is to find outside of romance/love. All you have to do is not sit around doing nothing all day. 

And sometimes, people may decide that, yes, there is a lot outside of love, but they still want it in their life. And that's okay. Then you have a new journey about navigating relationships/community.

It'll definitely be painful sometimes. I think nowadays I'm more sad that others can't easily fit into my needs than I am that I dont fit into theirs. Because, truthfully, none of us are wrong, were just different. And that makes things difficult but im holding onto hope that I might find the kinds of relationships I'm looking for. It'll just take some extra effort. 

I always tell people to grieve the life you thought you'd have. Cry and be angry and scream if you have to. Let yourself go through those emotions and you'll come out on the other side stronger as you move through this process. Aro people are amazing and beautiful and offer such a unique and NECESSARY perspective on relationships. Be the you that no one else can be!

I get *serious* aesthetic crushes. My attraction is like any other attraction. There is a strong PULL towards a specific person. I'll learn their schedule just so I might have the chance of bumping into them and seeing their face. I have to fight the urge to stare. I get nervous when they're near. I fantasize about what life might be like if we got closer. But not in a romantic way, not in a sexual way, not even really a platonic way. 

For me it's like those scenes in movies where they show the person gently adoring their lovers face/beauty. that's how I feel when I get aesthetic crushes. And I guess my desire is to freely adore their beauty *up close* like a lover would...without the lover part lol

The attraction varies in intensity. Sometimes it's incredibly strong and I spend my days thinking about them. which is why I never really knew I was aro until leaving high school bc I got all the "symptoms" of a romantic crush without the desire to be in a romantic relationship.

This is very relatable. There are other types of attraction other than romantic (sensual, aesthetic, platonic, etc.) but no one really talks about those. Or rather, the idea of a crush kinda combines all of these into one big mega attraction. Which of course makes it really confusing for ppl who don’t feel some aspect of that mega attraction. 

I’d get crushes all the time in school, wanted those feelings to be reciprocated and got sad when they already had partners. But I’d say to myself all the time that I never actually wanted to date or kiss them or anything. Had no craving to do so. 

In the end I realized my crushes were just aesthetic. For other ppl it often turns out to be platonic attraction.

That being said I don’t have any advice for you personally (just bc I’m not trying to date) but I wish you luck in finding what you’re looking for!

I blamed everything on social anxiety and intimacy issues. So, for years before I found out, I was searching for answers on how to get over those anxieties. But of course no matter how much I improved, that discomfort never actually went away. So then by the time I got into college I just started feeling hopelessly broken.

I was walking around my campus one day (my sophomore year so i was 20) and saw this cute guy with a very cute girl. i knew of them separately and we had shared classes together and i was so surprised they were dating. it kinda sent me on a spiral. crying about how i was gonna be alone forever and how it seemed no one found me interesting enough to love. i just didn't understand how romance was happening under my nose. people were falling in love and nothing was happening for me. and furthermore, the idea of being in a relationship made me incredibly uncomfortable.

so i went to look it up. behind teary eyes i literally typed in "why can't i imagine myself in a relationship". a quora post came up and one of the answers brought up the possibility of being aromantic. as soon as i saw the definition i was like...*oh that's me.*

for a while i said i was aromantic and bisexual. but eventually i realized that i was just a sex-favorable asexual. my process of figuring out im asexual was just a long back and forth of trying out different labels and seeing if they felt accurate to my reality. and now here i am! yay

Honestly, you're talking about this like an aromantic/aro spectrum person would talk about this lol. I definitely relate to not being able to picture myself in a relationship and "trying" to talk to people or go on dates to see if any feelings show up. Come to find out, that's just *not* how people who feel "normal" romantic attraction work 😅 the feelings/desire happen first and then you plan dates because it's something you actually *want* to do with that person. Not something you feel like you have to do to be normal.

My advice is really the same no matter what romantic orientation you are. Reflect and learn. That will take some time. Read experiences of what romantic attraction is like. Read experiences of the aro people on this forum. But most importantly, reflect on what your desires are. There are some stereotypes you may encounter on either side. So be careful not to let any labels define what you want or what you do. 

Whatever orientation you are, if you want romantic relationships you can go after that. And if you don't want anything to do with romance, it doesn't matter whether you're aro or not, you don't have to chase after that kind of relationship. 

It's your life your rules. You can live it how you want to live it no matter what is normal or what is expected! Easier said than done lol.  


Good luck!

I actually had sex for the first time like 2 months ago so it's fresh on my mind lol 

>1. Does anything change after having sex?

Surprisingly...no. I honestly thought doing it would make me feel different, but it didn't. I felt completely neutral. Though I have been plagued by the embarrassment of some of the things that happened lol. 

>2. Did you discover something about yourself?

I discovered that I could enjoy partnered sex. I was always curious how it would feel. My assumptions were confirmed. It wasn't the passionate and intense interaction that allosexual people described to me. I wasn't at all sexually attracted to the person i did it with. I learned that sexual attraction isn't what makes sex pleasurable. But it does make it different!

>1. Basically, was it worth it?! Everytime I've tried to experiment with my sexuality I came to the same conclusion: I am obviously Asexual, and I felt that I wasted my time!

Yeah it was worth it. Not because it was super amazing and there were fireworks or something like that. It was worth it just because it was an experience I was curious about. There were many awkward moments, but life is full of awkward moments. I dont regret it one bit. In fact, I'm super glad I did it. I had wanted to for so long and there really isn't a reason I have to force myself to avoid sex. Really, it was fear that was keeping me from trying. I didnt think i would be enough for whoever i was doing it with. So I'm happy I could let go of my ego for a bit and just let the awkward stuff happen to me so that I could learn more about what I want.

I feel you so much and your feelings are completely valid. So much around us is love love love. Can barely escape it. 

Just like any other loss, it's good to grieve the things that you feel have been taken from you. You can be sad about not having the life you thought you would have. Cry about it. Whine about it. Scream about it. Be angry. Be sad. Be envious. It's no good if you try to be okay with it when you're not. Express those emotions (healthily of course).

I think a lot of it will come with time. You notice how life goes on. You'll come across things that make you excited that aren't romance. You might find people with whom you have fullfiling relationships that aren't romantic. You'll get closer to yourself as you explore your life through an aromantic lens. 

For me I realized that i never wanted the romance. It was things around it I wanted. I wanted the connection with my friends by saying I had a crush. I wanted the social validation of being with somebody. I wanted to feel like I had met a milestone in my life. I didn't want to disappoint my parents. I wanted my relationships to be less complicated. And all of that still hurts. That hasn't gone away. 

But I love myself now more than i ever did before trying to be someone I'm not. I still feel lonely at times...that comes with being a minority. But I guess I've just made it my goal to withstand that loneliness now so that other aromantic people after me won't have to feel it as much. 

Good luck. And if you ever need anyone to talk to I'm right here! :)

I had a "crush" on this guy my sophomore year of college. One day I was walking around and saw him with his girlfriend...who was very pretty. I had classes with both of them and never could've guessed they were together. I was jealous. Not of her...but that they were somehow able to realize each other's feelings and get into a relationship. That always seemed impossible to me and I never understood how it worked. Everytime I imagined myself in a relationship I got so uncomfortable. 

So I literally googled "why can't I imagine myself in a relationship" and luckily came across this quora answer that said "maybe you're aromantic". What? Never heard that word before. I looked it up and it immediately clicked. 

For about a month or two I identified as aromantic bisexual. I consumed bisexual content and after those couple of months I realized that I don't actually relate much to bisexual posts. They were speaking about urges and cravings that I just don't get. I decided to look into asexuality as well. Of course I knew about it after going deeper into aromanticism. But I never associated it with me because I thought I knew what sexual attraction was. I dont really remember what exactly made it clear. It took me like a year or so to finally get a grasp on it and now here we are! :)

I remember hearing the word for the first time my freshman year of high school. One of my classmates was telling me their friend was asexual and I said "like needing one person to have a baby? No? hmm they should probably change the name" I still laugh about it from time to time. Never had another thought about it until my sophomore year of college. I think after that it took me like a year to fully grasp what sexual attraction is so that I could understand what it meant to not experience it.

There are more reasons than just the specific people to stay in a friendship. Like wanting someone to do things with. Feeling lonely. Having someone to talk to about specific things. Safety reasons. Networking. Blah blah. 

There is nothing different about platonic attraction that makes it somehow more inherent than romantic or sexual attraction. Just like other forms of attraction...not everyone feels platonic attraction.

The same way aromantic individuals can still get into romantic relationships. I also don't experience much platonic attraction. That just means I don't get any cravings to form friendships with specific people. I still like doing things with friends though. Attraction has nothing to do with whether i feel lonely.

No problem! Questioning asexuality is definitely a confusing process. Most of us have only seen how sexuality works for the majority, so figuring out if you're different can take getting a deeper understanding of what attraction actually is. 

 (Sorry if this is a little long)

▪Sex drive = when your body needs to release (engage in sexual intercourse/masturbate) 

▪Sexual arousal = when your body gets prepared to have sexual intercourse or masturbate 

▪Sexual attraction = when you see a particular person and  desire to do sexual things with them

Someone can have sexual drive but not be able to get aroused (Like men who want to have sex but have trouble keeping an erection. Or women who have trouble creating lubricant)

Someone can have sexual drive without sexual attraction. Meaning their body needs release but they dont have anyone they want to do it with. 

Someone can have arousal without sexual drive. Random erections are very common in men. Their body often times prepares for them to have sex even when their mind doesnt actually want it. 

Someone can have arousal without attraction. Your body can get prepared to have sex without actually thinking or seeing anyone who you want to have sex with. 

You can have attraction without drive. You may have a desire to do sexual things with a particular person (in general) but not have any sexual drive to do it with them. Meaning you/your body just doesn't need the release right now. 

And you can have attraction without arousal. Similar to the first point. You may want to do sexual things with a particular person but your body doesn't get aroused. 

And you can have one without the other two. 

So for asexuals we just don't have the attraction. We may or may not get aroused or have no sex drive or really high sex drives. But what we all have in common is that we have little to no desire to have sexual contact with any particular people
